A.why: Clear A-line gown with an elegant gold bodice and a candle-veil crown, but pale ivory and taupe drift towards linen and away from the night palette; the bulky banded sleeves are the widest thing from above.
A.fix: Slim the sleeves; make the skirt wine or deep gold over ivory; add shade-black at the hem; Neon on two candle spikes.

B.why: Strongest gown read: a wine bell skirt from the hip, a gold butterfly bodice, a candle crown; distinct from studded thanks to the bright gold front. Full-width wine sleeves make the top a broad slab, and the hem splays into flat bars from above.
B.fix: Slim the sleeves, darker with gold cuffs; close and round the hem; let shade-black creep up the front; Neon on the flame and the waist gem.

C.why: A fine open crown seen from above, but the body is a straight robe column with no waist; the gold hem basin reads as a tub, not a skirt.
C.fix: Replace the basin with a skirt flaring from the hip; cinch the waist; slim the sleeves and drop the cuff flare.

D.why: The splayed plate skirt reads as armour tassets; the wine sleeves on a gold torso put the emphasis at the shoulders. The halo ring is a good light idea.
D.fix: Rebuild the skirt as one continuous bell; make the sleeves match the bodice and slim them; keep the halo as Neon.

E.why: A gold box from shoulder to floor; the skirt is stepped cake tiers with no flare; the kimono wrap reads as a monk robe; the gold is oversaturated.
E.fix: Make one flaring skirt in wine with a single trim band; slim the sleeves; add height and a gem to the crown.

F.why: The sun-disc crown and ruff are the best invention in the wave and the front skirt flares prettily, but the whole set is one saturated gold, so from above it is a gold box; the striped panel and flare are front-only.
F.fix: Make the bodice and sleeves wine or dark gold and keep bright gold for trim; carry the flare and stripes round the back; add a shade-black creep; Neon on the sun disc.

notes: Every candidate keeps full shoulder-width block sleeves, so the brief's main flaw survives the whole wave; no one has slimmed the arms yet. B has the gown read and palette; A has the most elegant bodice; F has the best crown (sun disc) and ruff. The ideal mix: B's wine bell skirt and bodice, F's sun-disc crown and ruff, A's chain necklace, with slim sleeves. Glow is barely present in any set; souring (shade-black) is weak everywhere except B's back and underskirt.
